original_test_intent: For every RAID level supported and required by the system/controller specification, build an array from approved disposable drives, reboot, and verify correct BIOS/controller display without unresolved errors.
original_method: After critical approval, create each specified level using exact stable-identity members and settings through the supported BIOS/controller workflow, capture initialization, reboot once, verify BIOS and read-only controller/OS state, then clean up only under separate authorization.
manual_activity: User approves each level, exact disposable members and destructive disposition; qualified operator handles BIOS/KVM checkpoints; agent may execute only explicitly approved vendor actions and collect evidence.
required_inputs: Controller model/firmware and authoritative supported RAID-level matrix
Stripe, cache, initialization, hot spare and controller policy
Build order, array deletion/reinitialization and final-disposition plan
Backup, KVM/OOB, boot/data recovery, maintenance window and abort thresholds
safety_requirements: Resolve controller and every member by stable identity; exclude boot, management, production and unknown disks
Confirm each requested RAID level and RAID01 meaning are supported before creation
Preserve pre-state and do not clear logs
Stop on wrong target, unsupported level, initialization/controller/media/thermal error, degraded state, boot failure or recovery loss
Do not delete, initialize, rebuild, force online, repartition or repeat reboot outside the approved step
agent_execution_scope: Collect full controller, physical/virtual disk, boot and health baseline
Render exact vendor command or operator checklist for one approved level at a time
Capture creation, initialization, BIOS, post-reboot controller/OS/BMC evidence and expected-versus-observed layout
Do not choose members, authorize destruction, recover arrays automatically or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the supported level matrix, members/settings, destructive order and disposition
Provide BIOS/KVM operator and own controller/data/boot recovery
Review each level independently and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Read-only /c0 inventory cannot prove support, create any array, verify member settings, capture initialization or satisfy the rebooted BIOS checkpoint; assumed controller numbering is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each separately approved level, use a vendor-documented command or BIOS workflow bound to exact controller and member serials, then capture full create/init status and post-reboot BIOS plus read-only controller evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RAID 0/1/5/6/10/01 as supported, restart, BIOS verification and source 15/5 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each supported level as an isolated transaction with pre-authorized members, immutable before/after inventory and explicit teardown/final-state ownership.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds stable target guards and full lifecycle evidence while retaining every applicable RAID level and BIOS check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only automation assists validation but does not replace destructive creation or BIOS/KVM observation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Capacity, parity initialization and controller nomenclature vary; level names alone do not define member count, layout or readiness.

project_override_considerations: If the controller does not support RAID01 or uses a vendor-specific nested-level name, engineering must explicitly map or exclude it; the agent must not reinterpret it as RAID10.
expected_evidence: Critical approval and authoritative controller capability matrix
Exact per-level drive serial/slot/capacity and non-target exclusions
Full pre-state plus create/settings/initialization outputs and timestamps
Post-reboot BIOS screenshots and full controller physical/virtual inventory for every level
Boot/OS/mount, drive health/temperature and complete dmesg/syslog/SEL/BMC
Per-level teardown/final disposition, recovery notes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master clearly requires supported RAID creation and BIOS verification. DeepSeek's inventory-only output is a coverage failure, not a source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Capability matrix, disposable targets and recovery plan are supplyable destructive-test prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Restores destructive per-level creation, initialization and BIOS validation with exact member guards and final-state ownership.
independent_technical_reasoning: An existing-array inventory cannot validate creation logic or firmware support. Each RAID level changes data layout and usable capacity, and initialization may remain incomplete across reboot; therefore exact members/settings, controller-level creation evidence, readiness state and BIOS display must be proven separately before teardown or the next level.
